name: Dilation Clock
desc: A chunky pedestal clock on a brushed-steel plinth with a warm glowing face. Its hands turn

problems: You can tell at a glance it's a street or pedestal clock: a gold-rimmed glowing face, a dark column, a steel plinth and a gold finial. The colours fit the house look. In the scene it stands a little taller than the person, which is about right for a landmark.
It doesn't look 'chunky'. The column is only 26 wide under a face 100 across, so from a distance it reads like a thin lamppost. The 84-wide plinth also looks small under the face.
The arc at (0,-212) has a0=7 and a1=7, so its length is zero and it draws nothing. The idea of a slow-zone or dilation marker on the dial never appears.
Nothing in a single frame shows time dilation. The cue depends only on how fast the hands spin, so a still frame looks like any ordinary clock.
The halo circle (r62, alpha 0.18) makes a flat grey disc behind the face that looks a little muddy against the dark background.

for: Chunky pedestal clock with a glowing face whose hands tick slower near the beam and faster far away. It gives the world a visual cue for time dilation.

problems: Scale is wrong. The spec says h 2.7, but in the scene the clock comes up only to the person's waist or chest, about 1 m. It looks like a garden ornament, not a chunky city landmark.

The material doesn't match the brief. The plinth and the clock-head rim are rough, chipped grey stone, not brushed steel. The look is a rustic, mossy texture instead of the clean-shaded charcoal, brushed metal and gold house style.

There are stray shapes: a seashell on the ground at the bottom left, a clump of fern and grass, and loose rubble stones at the base. None of these belong to a city prop, and the shell reads as random clutter.
The face doesn't glow. It's a flat cream dial with no light coming off it, so the 'warm glowing face' never appears and the clock won't stand out at wide scale.
Nothing hints at time dilation. It's an ordinary Roman-numeral clock with no beam-facing cue and no motion streaks on the hands, so it can't carry the idea that time runs at different speeds.
The base is busy and uneven. Rocks and plants break the footprint, so the base doesn't sit as one clean, grounded block.
